axes_B: speech_vs_physical_act: speech, vocalization, or communication / bodily or physical act
inner_state_vs_outward_act: inner mental, perceptual, or affective state / outwardly performed act
same_act_vs_new_act: continues, elaborates, or completes the act already underway / introduces a separate, subsequent act or event
phase_of_the_event: onset or initiation / continuation or completion
act_vs_outcome: the act itself, or a further act / its result, consequence, or the state it leaves
act_vs_state: dynamic, bounded act or event / state, condition, posture, or unbounded activity
content_vs_discourse_marker: a contentful word naming an act or entity / a connective, temporal adverb, particle, hedge, or framing device
manner_vs_act: specifies the manner, means, path, or bodily shape of the act / names the act itself, without specifying how
kind_of_modifier: manner, quality, or spatial specification / time, sequence, frequency, or degree
argument_structure: self-standing in the slot (intransitive, bare, complete) / requires an object, complement, particle, or further clause
word_class_and_form: one word class or morphological form / another word class or morphological form
act_vs_entity: names the action or what it achieves / names a thing, person, instrument, or content involved in it
person_vs_thing_target: aimed at a person or addressee / aimed at an object, place, matter, or piece of information
self_vs_other_directed: engages or requires a second party / self-directed, self-contained, or undirected
engagement_vs_withdrawal: engaging, approaching, confronting, or staying with the matter at hand / withdrawing, departing, deflecting, or turning elsewhere
transfer_vs_own_handling: passing, giving, or supplying the thing to another party / acting on, keeping, or manipulating it oneself
motion_vs_stasis: motion, travel, or change of location / action involving no displacement
self_motion_vs_acting_on_object: the subject's own motion, posture, or bodily change / handling, placing, or moving an external object
force_and_harm: forceful, violent, abrupt, intense, or destructive / gentle, controlled, mild, or non-damaging
sexual_or_taboo_content: sexual, intimate, or otherwise taboo / non-sexual, everyday
bluntness_and_register: blunt, direct, colloquial naming / euphemistic, softened, or formal naming
specificity: broad, generic, or unmarked term / narrow, specific, or marked term
domain_specific_vs_general_purpose: act proper to the instrument, practice, or activity in play / general-purpose act usable of any situation
concreteness: concrete, tangible entity or bodily thing / abstract quality, attribute, or state of affairs
institutional_vs_personal: formal, legal, procedural, or collective channel / direct, personal, immediate act
action_vs_deliberation: a decisive, substantive act carried out / weighing, hedging, inquiring, or asking how to proceed
volition_and_agency: deliberate act the subject initiates and controls / involuntary reaction, state undergone, or another party's act
kind_of_inner_state: cognitive, epistemic, or perceptual (thinking, knowing, judging, noticing) / affective or volitional (feeling, wanting, needing, fearing)
kind_of_speech_act: informing, asserting, accepting, or committing / requesting, questioning, directing, doubting, or non-committal
assent_vs_refusal: affirming, assenting, or yielding / negating, refusing, or denying
evaluative_valence: positive, approving, benign / negative, aversive, condemnatory
creation_vs_destruction: bringing into being, adding, assembling, obtaining / ending, removing, dismantling, sending away
ritual_vs_ordinary: ritual, ceremonial, devotional, or performative act / ordinary practical act
which_member_of_the_field: one member or facet of the referential domain / a different member or facet of the same domain
spatial_configuration: a bounded goal, container, opening, or surface reached / an unbounded extent, interior, path, direction, or medium
realized_vs_prospective: what is or was the case — reported, accomplished, known / what is wanted, needed, required, or still to be done
appearance_vs_actuality: how it appears, seems, or is construed to be / what it actually is or intrinsically entails
notes_B:
37 axes. Every one of the 16 readers' 340 proposals is placed; nothing was dropped silently.

WHERE THE MERGES ARE SOFT (the seams a consumer should know about):

1. `same_act_vs_new_act` vs `phase_of_the_event`. Fourteen readers proposed continuation-vs-new-act and four proposed onset-vs-continuation; they are not the same contrast (one is "stays with this act / starts another", the other is "begins / finishes"), but many individual readings would sit plausibly on either. If you want fewer axes, these two collapse first and would take ~250 readings with them.

2. `act_vs_state` vs `act_vs_outcome`. Readers conflate these constantly — "action vs. resulting state", "process vs. product", "state or outcome vs. action or event" all straddle. I split them because "dynamic vs stative" and "the doing vs what it produced" are separable sentences, but individual readings will be assigned inconsistently across the boundary.

3. Three target-related axes — `person_vs_thing_target` (what kind of object), `self_vs_other_directed` (is there a second party at all), `engagement_vs_withdrawal` (stay with the target at hand or turn elsewhere) — are the hardest region. Several readers proposed two or all three under the same name ("target of the action" appears in readers 0, 4, 8 and 15 meaning three different things, which is why that string appears under three different axes here). If this region must be simplified, merge 1 and 2 and keep 3 separate; 3 is doing distinct work (it absorbs the literal toward/away motion readings as well as confront/avoid).

4. `argument_structure` vs `word_class_and_form`. I put complement-requirement and transitivity in the first and part-of-speech/inflection/number in the second. Readers 10 and 15 proposed them as one ("word class or syntactic frame"), and the split is a judgement call.

5. `specificity` vs `domain_specific_vs_general_purpose`. Kept apart because one is grain of reference (category vs instance, region vs part) and the other is fit to the practice in play (using the instrument properly vs a colourless verb). Five readers proposed the second; it would otherwise vanish into the first.

6. `sexual_or_taboo_content` vs `bluntness_and_register`. Content charge vs directness of wording. They co-occur (an explicit word is usually both), and `force_and_harm` also absorbed reader 15's "Transgressive force vs. restraint", which mixes violence and sexual charge into one pole.

FOLDED IN AS NARROWER READINGS (kept, but their distinctness is lost): "contact vs miss" (s6) → act_vs_outcome, though it is really success-of-the-act; "handling vs non-handling" (s6) and "handling the object vs. not handling it" (s12) and "bodily contact" (s8) → speech_vs_physical_act, whose non-physical pole therefore covers both speech and no-contact acts; "additive vs. restrictive continuation" (s1) is a within-connective contrast with no home of its own; "means vs. end" (s5, s13) sits under act_vs_entity on the instrument side only; "manner vs. path" (s4) went to manner_vs_act rather than spatial_configuration; "perception vs. cognition" (s11) fits kind_of_inner_state badly — its poles are not the cognitive/affective ones; "gender" (s2) and "place type" (s1) are field-member readings with no field in common.

WHAT I SUSPECT IS MISSING. (a) Nothing here names the contrast between a filler that is *apt* to the frame and one that is semantically anomalous or only figuratively applicable — readers 0 ("frame fit") and 13 ("literal specific vs generic figurative") gesture at it and I dispersed them into syntax and specificity respectively. (b) Number of participants / collectivity appears only inside institutional_vs_personal via s15's "Collective vs. individual". (c) No axis tracks language or script, which given CJK surfaces in this corpus may be a real gap. (d) `evaluative_valence`, `assent_vs_refusal`, `appearance_vs_actuality` and `realized_vs_prospective` each rest on two readers; they are the four most likely to be noise rather than structure, and the first to cut if the vocabulary must shrink.

Finally: 46 readings were explicitly placed nowhere by their own readers (reader 9 alone declined 13, reader 5 twelve), so the merge cannot be checked against a full partition of the 2,466.
